title: Tokenization — Cut a Sentence into Reusable Pieces
key_insight: A tokenizer splits text into tokens and assigns each token a number. A token may be a word, part of a word, punctuation, or even a byte.
body:
## Cut a Sentence into Reusable Pieces

A model receives “unbelievable,” but it cannot store every possible word anyone might invent. It needs a smaller set of reusable pieces.

A tokenizer splits text into tokens and assigns each token a number. A token may be a word, part of a word, punctuation, or even a byte.

The model sees token numbers, not raw letters. Decoding later joins predicted tokens back into readable text.
common_mistakes: A tokenizer directly verifies every factual answer.
Every token is always one complete English word.
Token numbers have the same meaning across all models.
mini_exercise: Draw “Cut a Sentence into Reusable Pieces” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Every language-model input and output passes through a tokenizer, so its choices affect meaning, length, and cost.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Cut a Sentence into Reusable Pieces,” explain Tokenization without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
